name: Isolde Mwangi-Petrov
description:
Isolde Mwangi-Petrov spent eighteen years in Axiom CorpSec, rising to Senior Investigator in the Special Investigations Division — the unit that handles crimes too complex or sensitive for regular corporate security. She was good at her job. She was also naive enough to believe that being good at her job meant the job was good.

The break came when she uncovered evidence that her own division was systematically fabricating cases against Shelf residents to meet arrest quotas and justify budget allocations. She reported it through proper channels. The proper channels destroyed the evidence, transferred her to a desk, and began building a case to discredit her. She resigned before they could fire her, took everything she could carry — physically and mentally — and set up shop as a freelance investigator dedicated to the cases CorpSec won't touch or can't be trusted with.

Now she operates from Meridian Station, deliberately choosing neutral ground because every corporate territory is hostile territory for her. Her clients are typically people who have been wronged by corporate power and have nowhere else to turn — employees who've witnessed crimes, families of people disappeared by CorpSec, whistleblowers who need evidence collected before they're silenced. She is effective because she knows exactly how the machine works from the inside, and she is dangerous to the corporations because she knows where the bodies are buried. Axiom has made three attempts to buy her silence. The fourth attempt, she suspects, won't involve money.
affiliation: Independent — former Axiom CorpSec Special Investigations Division
location: A rented office in Meridian Station, chosen for its neutral-ground status — no corporation claims jurisdiction in the transit nexus, near State and Jackson
specialization: Cases involving corporate misconduct, CorpSec corruption, and institutional abuse of power
methods: Leveraging insider knowledge of CorpSec procedures, blind spots, and jurisdictional gaps
Running informant networks inside corporate security divisions
Exploiting the bureaucratic friction between competing corporate jurisdictions
Forensic document analysis — detecting fabricated corporate records
Conducting parallel investigations that mirror CorpSec methodology but aren't bound by corporate loyalty
notable_cases: Proved that Axiom CorpSec had been framing Shelf residents for crimes committed by corporate employees — a case that earned her the nickname 'The Defector' and a permanent Axiom blacklist
Investigated the disappearance of a Tessera researcher and discovered they'd been disappeared by their own company's security for threatening to publish safety data
Exposed a CorpSec protection racket operating in the Narrows, where officers were charging residents for 'security services' that amounted to not harassing them
equipment: CorpSec-grade encrypted communicator — kept from her time on the force, modified to prevent tracking
Database of CorpSec operational codes, patrol schedules, and jurisdictional maps — increasingly outdated but still valuable
Body armor disguised as civilian clothing — CorpSec issue, custom-fitted
A badge she kept — has no legal authority but opens psychological doors
Counter-forensics kit for cleaning scenes of her own presence
personality: Isolde is the kind of ex-cop who left the force because she took the job too seriously, not because she didn't take it seriously enough. She is forty-four, tall, Kenyan-Russian heritage with bronze skin and prematurely gray hair she wears in a severe bun. She carries herself with the posture and watchfulness of someone trained to assess threat levels in every room, and she still reflexively identifies exits and cover positions. She is angry — a slow, controlled anger at the system she used to serve and now understands was never designed to serve people like her. She drinks whiskey and regrets in equal measure, trusts almost nobody, and takes cases that other PIs won't touch because they involve going up against corporate security apparatus.

relationships.name: Captain Vuk Haugen-Diarra
relationships.description: Still inside Axiom CorpSec, feeding her information at enormous personal risk — the only person from her old life she still trusts

relationships.name: Nkechi Rojas-Gyasi
relationships.description: A Shelf community organizer whose brother Isolde proved was framed by CorpSec — now helps Isolde connect with clients who need her

story_hooks: Captain Vuk goes silent — either he's been compromised or he's been turned, and Isolde has to determine which without exposing herself to CorpSec
Axiom hires a different PI to investigate Isolde, building a case to have her detained on fabricated charges — she has to investigate her own investigator

A former colleague from Special Investigations contacts her claiming to have evidence of a CorpSec operation so illegal it could bring down an entire corporate board — but the colleague was involved in the operation against Isolde years ago, and trust is impossible

physical_description.build: Athletic and lean, muscled in the shoulders and forearms from years of fieldwork — controlled tension in her frame rather than bulk
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with silver threading at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a tight, practical braid that extends to mid-back; no-nonsense styling
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium-warm complexion, even tone reflecting both East African and Slavic ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Sharp cheekbones, defined jawline, minimal makeup — a face that reads as professional and uncompromising. Small scar through her left eyebrow from a fieldwork incident. No visible sun damage; maintains herself carefully
distinguishing_marks: Thin scar through left eyebrow, approximately 2cm, from a struggle during her CorpSec days
Faint burn mark on the inside of her right wrist, roughly the size of a cigarette tip — from a threat that escalated into intimidation
Axiom corporate tattoo on her right shoulder blade (a geometric sigil) that she has chosen not to remove — a reminder and a warning to herself
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None visible. Her augmentations are subcutaneous: a neural interface array behind her left ear (invisible under hair), optical enhancements (undetectable to casual observation), and an encrypted data vault implanted in her molars. She runs clean and quiet — no chrome, no LEDs, no tells.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate economy. Shoulders slightly forward, weight balanced on the balls of her feet even when seated — someone trained to move quickly if needed. Her gaze is direct and measuring; she watches before she speaks. Tense at baseline, but controlled — the calm of someone who has learned that showing fear is a liability
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 professional-tactical hybrid. Dark neutral tones: charcoal, black, grey. Fitted synthetic-leather jacket with reinforced elbows (Meridian Station brand, durable), functional cargo pants with multiple pockets and tool loops, sturdy polymer-soled boots broken in from field work. A silver pendant watch on her wrist — old, not smart-enabled, deliberately analog. She dresses to move, not to impress. No visible branding except the watch. Her office clothes are as functional as her field clothes — no performance necessary.

image_prompt: Isolde Mwangi-Petrov, 40-year-old East African-Russian woman, athletic lean build, dark hair braided back with silver at temples, sharp cheekbones, alert deep brown eyes, minimal makeup, professional but worn. Wearing fitted dark charcoal synthetic-leather jacket with reinforced elbows, dark tactical cargo pants, sturdy black boots. Sitting at a desk in a dim Meridian Station office lit by cool blue neon, hands folded, direct unreadable gaze toward camera. Cyberpunk noir, gritty and composed, no chrome augmentations visible but underlying intensity of someone who knows too much. Moody overhead lighting creating shadows across her face, slight scar visible through left eyebrow. Analog watch on wrist. Mood: dangerous competence, moral conviction, corporate-haunted. --ar 2:3 --v 6
